_note: Thomas, 2026-09-06: 'chase all of the round 3 leads' — the cheapest of them. Two UN standards that every national trade release and every government-finance release in this corpus could cite were simply absent, each already quoted at A grade by a document read during round 2: IMTS (the trade-statistics sibling of SNA 2008 and BPM6) and COFOG (the expenditure-by-function sibling of COICOP, which the corpus already carries). This slice mints both and wires whatever the national methodology documents actually say — which turned out to be much less than the leads suggested, because most trade and GFS publishers describe themselves as following 'international standards' or 'United Nations recommendations' without ever naming the manual. Both editions were established by reading UNSD rather than assumed: COFOG's current operational version is the 1999 revision (UNSD registry: Year Adopted 1999, Year Published 2000; a further revision is not expected before 2028), and IMTS 2010 is still current (a successor referred to by UNSD as IMTS 2026 was not yet adopted when this was read). Every url and evidence_url was raw-verified HTTP 200 and every quote re-fetched and substring-checked against the live cited URL after this file was written.

reports.title: International Merchandise Trade Statistics: Concepts and Definitions 2010
reports.publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Statistics Division
reports.description: The United Nations' global recommendation for compiling and disseminating statistics on trade in goods, issued as Statistical Papers Series M No. 52, Revision 3 and superseding Revision 2 of 1998. It sets the definitions national compilers use for coverage, the general and special trade systems, statistical territory, valuation, quantity measurement, partner-country attribution and commodity classification, harmonised as far as possible with the recommendations for trade in services, balance of payments and national accounts. It is the trade-statistics counterpart of SNA 2008 and BPM6.
reports.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. A standing recommendation revised roughly once a decade: Revision 2 (1998) superseded by IMTS 2010 (Revision 3, published 2011), which UNSD's methodology page still listed as the current Concepts and Definitions volume when read on 2026-09-06. A successor UNSD refers to as IMTS 2026 was in preparation and not yet adopted.
title_aliases: Estadísticas del Comercio Internacional de Mercancías

reports.title: Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG)
reports.description: The United Nations classification of government outlays by function or socio-economic objective — general public services, defence, public order and safety, economic affairs, environmental protection, housing and community amenities, health, recreation, education and social protection. It is one of the four classifications of expenditure according to purpose published together as Statistical Papers Series M No. 84, alongside COICOP, COPNI and COPP. First published in 1980 and revised in 1999, it is the functional breakdown embedded in SNA 2008, ESA 2010 and the IMF's GFSM 2014, and the one national government-finance releases either apply directly or adapt into a national variant.
reports.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. Structural revision only: first published 1980, revised 1999 (the current operational version; UNSD's registry records Year Adopted 1999, Year Published 2000). A revision is under way under the UN Committee of Experts' Task Team on COFOG, which UNSD anticipates completing by 2028.

_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-09-06, and the resolution is a routing finding worth more than the edge. This entry originally parked the edge because www.imf.org returns HTTP 403 (Akamai) to a browser-UA curl on every PDF path tried, from both of this session's networks, while Chrome navigates to the same PDF fine but lands it in Chrome's PDF viewer where get_page_text cannot reach it. Thomas pointed at elibrary.imf.org, which is a DIFFERENT HOST and is wide open: `?bot=bot` on a browse or search URL returns full HTML, and `https://www.elibrary.imf.org/downloadpdf/display/book/<isbn>/<isbn>.pdf` serves complete manuals to a plain curl (GFSM 2014 English, 5.4MB, HTTP 200). The whole IMF family is therefore readable: the corpus carries imf-gfsm, imf-bpm6, imf-mfsmcg-2016, imf-psds-guide, imf-dqaf, imf-weo, imf-fiscal-monitor, imf-gfsr and imf-sdds, none of which had a readable primary source before today. Two traps for whoever works that seam: each manual has one ISBN PER LANGUAGE and the search results do not say which is which (for GFSM 2014, 9781498343763 is English and 9781484383391 is Chinese), and the manuals are two-column, so `pdftotext -layout` interleaves them and plain pdftotext reading order is what produces quotable spans. The edge this entry was about is now live, along with imf-gfsm -> sna-2008 found in the same read.

REFUSED 2026-09-06 on edition, not on evidence.
